evidence: The thickness of the deposited films was analyzed by spectroscopic ellipsometry using an alpha-SE ellipsometer (J.A Woollam Co. Inc.) and by X-ray reflectivity (XRR) using an AXS D8 Discover (Bruker). The X-ray reflectivity data were fitted using the GenX software and the ellipsometer data were fitted to a Cauchy function. XRR was further used to determine the density of the deposited films. The deposited films were studied using X-ray diffraction in grazing incidence (GI-XRD) and q–2q configuration using a D5000 (Siemens) diffractometer equipped with a Gölbel mirror providing parallel Cu-Kα radiation. The film roughness was analyzed by atomic force microscopy (AFM) using a XE-70 (Park Systems) in non-contact mode. X-ray fluorescence (XRF) was used to determine the composition of iron and phosphorus in the deposited films using a Philips PW2400 spectrometer and UniQuant analysis software. The electrochemical properties of the deposited samples were investigated in CR2032 coin cells. Cyclic voltammetry measurements were carried out in the range 2.3 –4.0 V with a scanning rate of 0.1 mV s⁻¹. The galvanostatic data were measured during charge –discharge cycles at a current rate close to 1C (181 mA g⁻¹) over the voltage range 2.0 –4.0 V with 5 min relaxation time after each cycle.
